plain_english_policy: This bill creates two new criminal offenses related to firearm transactions. First, it makes it a Class C felony for anyone who knowingly asks or encourages a licensed dealer or private seller to sell a gun when the person knows that sale would break state or federal law. Second, it is also a Class C felony to give false information about a transaction's legality with the intent to deceive the seller. The bill explicitly excludes peace officers acting in their official capacity from these charges.
policy_direction_if_enacted: Enactment establishes new crimes targeting individuals who facilitate illegal firearm transfers by soliciting dealers or providing deceptive information, thereby increasing penalties for bad-faith interactions with gun sellers while exempting law enforcement officials performing duties.
sponsorship_supports_position: Representatives Hurst, Johnson (R), Oden, Morrow, Hill, Galliher, Greeson and Thomas
evidence_quotes: "A person who knowingly solicits, persuades, encourages, or entices a licensed dealer or private seller of a firearm or ammunition to transfer a firearm or ammunition under circumstances which the person knows would violate the laws of this state or the United States is guilty of a Class C felony."

"A person who provides to a licensed dealer or private seller of firearms or ammunition what the person knows to be materially false information with intent to deceive the dealer or seller about the legality of the transfer of a firearm or ammunition is guilty of a Class C felony."
review_reason: The bill text clearly defines new crimes and penalties without ambiguity.
